claims.text: The proposed intervention is to deposit a thin, continuous Al2O3 layer between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
An interfacial Al2O3 layer will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion with the Al2O3 layer will prevent premature coating failure.
The Al2O3-modified coating will maintain corrosion protection during subcritical-water operation at approximately 300–400°C.
The Al2O3-modified coating will maintain protection during accident-relevant steam exposure up to approximately 1200°C for several hours.
The deposited Al2O3 layer will be thin, dense, and physically continuous at the Cr–Zr interface.
Al2O3 has low diffusivity for chromium under the stated elevated-temperature conditions.
Al2O3 has low diffusivity for zirconium under the stated elevated-temperature conditions.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will minimize the formation of brittle Cr–Zr intermetallic phases.
Minimizing interdiffusion and brittle intermetallic formation will preserve Cr-coating integrity and adhesion.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating on zirconium alloy is susceptible to premature elevated-temperature failure caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the Al2O3-modified system will show significantly less Cr penetration into the zirconium substrate.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the Al2O3-modified system will form fewer Cr–Zr intermetallic phases.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the Al2O3-modified system will retain better coating integrity and mechanical adhesion after the specified exposures.
The long-term stability of the Al2O3 barrier during variable thermal cycling and possible chemical interaction with Cr over multi-year reactor service is uncertain.
